votes.motion: Approve the work session meeting minutes of March 4, 2025 and March 18, 2025.
votes.description: The Council approved the official work session meeting minutes from March 4, 2025 and March 18, 2025.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing and refer Items B1 through B4 to a future Consent Agenda.
votes.description: The Council closed the public hearing on four grant applications (Homeless Shelter Cities Mitigation, Youth Advocacy Anti-Drug Coalition, Summer Food Service Program, and Internet Crimes Against Children) and referred them to a future consent agenda for action.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing and approve the following changes to the CIP budget: remove the second tranche of Public Lands GO Bonds from the Key Changes document; allow the Administration to use $300,000 for CPTED lighting; all other funding will be discussed at the briefings as scheduled and approved at the August 19th Council Meeting.
votes.description: The Council closed the public hearing on the FY2026 Capital Improvement Program and approved interim CIP budget changes, with remaining project-specific funding allocations to be finalized at the August 19th meeting.

votes.motion: Adopt Ordinance 47 of 2025, approving the Mixed-Use Zoning consolidation petition and accompanying ordinances including a geographically specific stepback in the Sugar House additional height area, setting the effective date three months after adoption, and adopting legislative actions to review interior block study for potential downzones, update the Central Community master plan, review on-street parking policies, and request the administration review standards for new construction adjacent to contributing structures in historic districts.
votes.description: The Council adopted the Mixed-Use Zoning Consolidation ordinance that consolidates up to 27 existing zoning districts into six new mixed-use districts, with specific stepback requirements in the Sugar House area and a three-month delayed effective date, along with several legislative intent actions for follow-up reviews.

votes.motion: Adopt Resolution 19 of 2025, naming the northeast baseball field at Riverside Park as the "Neil Draper Field".
votes.description: The Council adopted a resolution renaming the northeast baseball field at Riverside Park in honor of Neil Draper, a community member and business owner who made significant contributions to Rose Park Baseball before his passing in March 2025.

The Council adopted the full consent agenda, which included setting public hearing dates for a Truth-in-Taxation hearing, Design Review Standards Amendment, Parking Regulations Downtown Text Amendment, and Chapter 11.14 Parties/Gatherings ordinance amendment, as well as approving board appointments for Sarah Vaughn and Margaret Neville to the Library Board and Solomon Brumbaugh to the Transportation Advisory Board.
